chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me said: Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq al-Tajir narrated to me, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Ahwal, the companion of al-Taqq, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said in a long narration:

Affairs are of three types: an affair whose guidance is clear to you, so follow it; and an affair whose deviation is clear to you, so avoid it; and an affair about which there is difference (doubt), so refer it back to God, the Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of affairs according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Khisal establishes the tripartite epistemological framework for distinguishing between definitive rulings (qat'i), probable ones (zanni), and ambiguous matters (mushkilat). It underscores the Shia methodological principle of returning to divine authority or the Imams when clarity is absent, serving as a precursor to the development of usul al-fiqh. The classification provides a practical roadmap for navigating religious obligations and theological uncertainties with precision and humility.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-189 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq al-Tajir, on the authority of Ali ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Al-Ahval Sahib al-Taq Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-No’man), on the authority of Jamil ibn Salih, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said as part of a long narration, “
There are three types of affairs: ones that are clearly right and you can follow; ones that are clearly wrong and you should avoid; and ones that are doubtful which you must leave up to God.”
